claim.pdf_says: BLOCK CONTAINS [integer-1 TO] integer-2 {RECORDS / CHARACTERS} (RECORDS underlined; CHARACTERS printed without underline)
claim.why_it_matters: Underlining added: per §1985:IV.2.1.2 an uppercase word not underlined is optional. The printed BLOCK CONTAINS clause (sequential FD, V-9) leaves CHARACTERS un-underlined (the implicitly selected choice that may be omitted, e.g. BLOCK CONTAINS 80); the markdown makes it a required key word, falsely restrictive syntax. Page 203's transcription of the same clause correctly leaves it plain.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered page 201 (V-9) at 300 dpi and cropped the BLOCK CONTAINS choice braces: RECORDS carries an underline, CHARACTERS has none. The markdown (page-201.md line 18) writes <u>CHARACTERS</u>, which turns an optional word (the implicitly selected brace option) into a key word, so the transcription states falsely restrictive syntax. The claim quotes both sources accurately.
